info.short_description: Flu (seasonal influenza vaccine, 2019-20 onward) or rsv (maternal RSV vaccine, 2025-26).
info.long_description: Vaccine the estimate refers to. For flu, seasonal influenza vaccine received before or during pregnancy since July 1 of the season. For rsv, RSV vaccine (Abrysvo) received during pregnancy, recommended at 32-36 weeks' gestation during September through January.

info.short_description: Overall or one of nine CDC race and ethnicity groups (e.g. White, NH; Black, NH; Hispanic/Latino; Asian, NH; Unknown).
info.long_description: Race and ethnicity of the pregnant women in the estimate, using CDC's labels: Overall, American Indian / Alaska Native, NH; Asian, NH; Black, NH; Hispanic/Latino; Middle Eastern or North African; Multiple/Other, NH; Native Hawaiian / Pacific Islander, NH; White, NH; and Unknown. NH stands for non-Hispanic. Overall includes women with unknown race and ethnicity.

info.long_name: Cumulative percent of pregnant women 18-49 vaccinated
info.short_description: Percent of women 18-49 with a pregnancy this season who had received the vaccine as of the week ending date, in Vaccine Safety Datalink health systems.
info.long_description: Cumulative percent of women ages 18-49 with a pregnancy during the season who had received the vaccine as of the week ending date, from electronic health records of the integrated health systems in the Vaccine Safety Datalink (10 sites). For flu, the denominator is women pregnant at any point in the season (August through March) and the numerator counts flu vaccines received since July 1 before or during pregnancy. For RSV, the denominator is women who reached 32 weeks' gestation since September 1 and the numerator counts RSV vaccines received during pregnancy. Women stay in both numerator and denominator after the pregnancy ends, and newly identified pregnancies enter the denominator over time, so cumulative coverage can fall from one week to the next. Vaccines given outside a VSD site may be missed, so coverage may be underestimated. National only; VSD members are not a representative sample of U.S. pregnant women.

vsd.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
vsd.location: Percent of Pregnant Women Ages 18-49 Years Who Have Received an Influenza (or RSV) Vaccine, by Race and Ethnicity (FluVaxView and RSVVaxView dashboards)
vsd.description: The Vaccine Safety Datalink (VSD) is a collaboration between CDC's Immunization Safety Office and integrated health care organizations that use their electronic health records to study vaccine safety. CDC uses the VSD to publish weekly cumulative influenza vaccination coverage among pregnant women ages 18-49 (2019-20 season onward) and, since 2023-24, RSV vaccination coverage among pregnant women reaching 32 weeks' gestation, overall and by race and ethnicity. The current dashboards use 10 reporting sites for every season (earlier archived data used 8). Coverage is national only, describes VSD members rather than a representative sample, can be revised as pregnancies are identified, and may miss vaccines given outside the health system.
vsd.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.
